seed.relationship: two women who once shared a stage
seed.conflict: about a promise nobody remembers making
seed.topicSeed: a shoe repair stall in Tbilisi; two women who once shared a stage about a promise nobody remembers making

g.passage: "Mend the heel, and I will pay you when we sing again," Stanislav said, setting one worn slipper on my counter. I am Dmitri; I fix shoes now in a stall near the old bridge in Tbilisi, but twenty years ago she and I shared a stage at the opera house, two sopranos who had sworn, she insists, to sing our duet together once more before we grew old. I remember the opera house, the dust of the footlights, the way she tapped her toe before every entrance. I do not remember the vow. I hammered the heel while she hummed the opening bars, slightly flat, and waited for me to join. My throat was full of leather dust and doubt. Still, when she reached the high phrase, I heard my own voice catch it, rusty but whole, and the man at the next stall put down his knife to listen.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: The narrator recounts a past performance and then explains why she gave up singing for shoe repair.
A visitor invokes a shared pledge, the narrator doubts it, and she then acts as though it holds.
The narrator describes her stall at length and then contrasts it with a crowded opera house.
Two former singers argue over a vow, and one leaves the stall before it is resolved.
g.explanation: 지문은 Stanislav가 함께 노래하자던 약속을 꺼내며 시작하고, 화자는 그 약속을 기억하지 못한다고 의심을 드러낸 뒤, 결국 그녀의 노래에 목소리를 보태며 약속이 유효한 듯 행동한다. 따라서 '약속 제시 → 의심 → 행동으로 수용'의 흐름을 말한 B가 정답이다. A는 신발 수선을 하게 된 이유가 설명되지 않으므로 틀리다. C는 가게 묘사가 길지 않고 대비 구조도 아니다. D는 두 사람이 다투거나 누군가 떠나는 장면이 없다.

seed.topicSeed: a hospital waiting room in Maui; twin brothers dividing a house over who should stay behind

g.passage: When Rangi arrived at the hospital in Wailuku, his twin, Anahera, had already claimed the chair nearest the nurses' desk, a clipboard of their father's forms on his knee. For an hour they spoke only of parking and vending machines. Then Anahera began listing the rooms of the house in Paia: the lanai, the workshop, the bedroom with the warped door. He had been dividing it in his head, Rangi realized, deciding who would sell and who would stay on with the old man. Rangi had assumed the answer for years: the brother who never left would simply keep staying. But watching Anahera's thumb worry the edge of the clipboard, he saw how tired that brother was. So when the nurse called their name, it was Rangi who stood first, and on the drive home he asked which room had the better light.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: It describes the waiting room closely, then recalls a childhood memory that both brothers still share.
It presents an argument between the brothers, then shows a nurse settling their dispute.
It moves from small talk to a hidden question about the house, then to one brother's changed view.
It lists the rooms of a house, then explains why the brothers agree to sell the property.
g.explanation: 지문은 주차·자판기 같은 잡담에서 시작해 Anahera가 집의 방들을 나열하며 누가 남을지라는 숨은 질문으로 초점을 옮긴다. 이어 Rangi는 형제의 피로를 보고 오랜 가정을 바꾼다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A의 어린 시절 회상, B의 다툼과 간호사의 중재, D의 매각 합의는 지문에 없다.

seed.relationship: two neighbors with a shared wall
seed.openingStyle: 과거를 회상하는 문장으로 시작('Years later', 'Once' 등)
seed.topicSeed: a train compartment in Kerala; two neighbors with a shared wall over an unfinished project

g.passage: Years later, Kamala still told the story of the night train from Kochi to Kozhikode, when she found herself sharing a compartment with Tara, the neighbor whose kitchen backed onto her own. For a decade the two households had been painting a mural along their common wall, a river in turquoise and ochre, and for two years it had stopped at a half-finished heron. Neither woman had said why. In the swaying dark, Tara admitted she had run out of the blue she liked and was ashamed to ask for money. Kamala laughed so loudly that the ticket collector peered in. She had stopped, she confessed, because she believed Tara had grown tired of her. By the time the coconut palms turned gray with dawn, they had sketched the heron's other wing on the back of a ticket.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
options: A description of a long journey is followed by an account of the scenery at sunrise.
A disagreement between neighbors is introduced and then settled with a passing stranger's help.
A mural's history is traced from its beginning to the day it was finally completed.
A stalled shared project is introduced, and then each woman's hidden reason is revealed.
g.explanation: 지문은 먼저 두 이웃이 함께 그리던 벽화가 2년째 멈춰 있다는 상황을 제시한다. 이어 Tara는 물감 값을 말하기 부끄러웠다고, Kamala는 Tara가 자신에게 싫증 났다고 여겼다고 각자 숨긴 이유를 털어놓는다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 여정 묘사가 중심이 아니고, B의 낯선 사람(검표원)은 갈등을 풀지 않으며, C는 벽화가 완성되지 않는다.

seed.relationship: a pair of lifelong friends who rarely speak
seed.conflict: when a visitor arrives and sees what the family does not
seed.topicSeed: a rented farmhouse in Hanoi; a pair of lifelong friends who rarely speak when a visitor arrives and sees what the family does not

g.passage: Anh does not talk at breakfast. I learned this my first morning in the farmhouse his family rents outside Hanoi, where I had come as a guest of his sister. Tamar, his friend since childhood, sat across from him, and the two of them passed the fish sauce and the chili without a word. His mother apologized for them, calling them two stones. But I watched more closely. __When Tamar's cup ran low, Anh's hand was already on the teapot before she reached for it.__ Later, in the yard, Tamar knelt to retie a sandal strap that had come loose on Anh's foot, and he simply lifted his heel to help. Nobody else at the table seemed to notice. By noon the heat had pressed the rice fields into a single green sheet.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It gives an early sign that the friends' silence hides close attention, which a later scene confirms.
It suggests that Anh resents serving Tamar, a feeling that his mother tries hard to hide from the guest.
It shows that the narrator misreads the friends' habits, an error the yard scene later corrects.
It introduces a rivalry between the two friends that grows sharper as the morning goes on.
g.explanation: 밑줄 문장은 Tamar가 손을 뻗기도 전에 Anh가 찻주전자를 드는 장면으로, 침묵 속에 세심한 배려가 있음을 처음 보여 준다. 이후 마당에서 Tamar가 샌들 끈을 묶어 주고 Anh가 발꿈치를 들어 주는 장면이 이를 다시 확인한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 원망, C의 화자의 오해, D의 경쟁 관계는 지문 근거가 없다.

seed.conflict: over a repair that could never really fix it
seed.topicSeed: a customs checkpoint in Tehran; a pair of rival bakers over a repair that could never really fix it

g.passage: What could a soldier at the city gate know of bread? Farhad wondered this as the customs man poked a rod through his sacks of flour, the same sacks Mehrnaz, his rival from across the bazaar, had sent back to him that morning with a mended seam. Last winter he had spread word that her ovens were cracked; her trade had never quite recovered. The seam was the work of a careful needle, small even stitches in red thread, her family's color. __He understood that a single sack, however finely sewn, could not undo what a whole season of rumor had done.__ The soldier waved him through. Farhad did not move at once. He turned the cart around, toward her shop rather than his own, while the mule complained and the gate lanterns swung in the wind.
g.question: Which choice best describes the function of the underlined sentence in the text as a whole?
options: It reveals that Farhad believes Mehrnaz mended the sack in order to mock him in front of the bazaar.
It marks Farhad's sense that her gesture cannot match his harm, setting up his turn.
It explains why the soldier distrusts Farhad's flour and delays his passage.
It suggests that Farhad plans to repay Mehrnaz by spreading a new rumor.
g.explanation: 앞부분에서 Farhad는 지난겨울 Mehrnaz의 오븐에 대한 소문을 퍼뜨려 그녀의 장사를 망쳤고, 그녀는 오히려 자루를 정성껏 꿰매 돌려보냈다. 밑줄 문장은 그 작은 친절이 자신의 해악을 상쇄할 수 없다는 깨달음을 보여 주고, 이것이 그녀의 가게로 수레를 돌리는 행동으로 이어진다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 조롱, C의 병사의 불신, D의 새 소문은 지문과 맞지 않는다.

seed.relationship: a shopkeeper and a persistent customer
seed.openingStyle: 구체적인 사물이나 동작으로 시작(관사 The 로 시작하지 말 것)
seed.topicSeed: a seaside promenade in Vermont; a shopkeeper and a persistent customer while waiting for important news

g.passage: Canvas awnings snapped over Piper's souvenir stand on the Burlington promenade, where the lake wind smelled almost like the sea. Every afternoon Despina came to ask whether the postcards had changed. They had not. She bought one anyway, always the same lighthouse, and stood turning it over while she watched the ferry dock, waiting for word about her son's surgery in Boston. Piper, who had a dozen sharp ways to say that the rack was the rack, never used them. One might call the purchases foolish, and the gulls, at least, seemed to. But a woman who buys the same lighthouse eleven days running is not shopping; she is keeping a lamp lit, and Piper, to her credit, understood the difference. At four the ferry horn sounded, and the gulls rose all at once from the railing.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Despina's daily visits?
options: Amused contempt for a customer who keeps wasting money on identical cards.
Detached indifference that reports the visits without any judgment.
Impatient disapproval of a customer who distracts Piper from work.
Gentle sympathy that finds a hopeful ritual in a seemingly odd habit.
g.explanation: 서술자는 같은 등대 엽서를 매일 사는 행동을 어리석다고 볼 수도 있다고 인정하면서도, 그것을 아들의 소식을 기다리며 등불을 지키는 일로 재해석한다. 또한 날카로운 말을 아끼는 Piper를 칭찬하여 Despina에 대한 따뜻한 시선을 드러낸다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A의 경멸과 C의 못마땅함은 서술자의 재해석과 맞지 않고, B는 서술자가 분명한 평가를 내리므로 틀리다.

seed.setting: a movie theater in the off-season
seed.relationship: an old teacher and a former pupil
seed.topicSeed: a movie theater in the off-season in Albuquerque; an old teacher and a former pupil after a misunderstood gift

g.passage: Stale butter and dust hang in the lobby of the old theater on Central Avenue in February, when you are the only one buying a ticket. You came because Mr. Lior, your old chemistry teacher, wrote to say he runs the projector now. Twelve years ago you gave him a framed periodic table for his retirement, and he set it face down on his desk without a word; you took it as an insult and stopped writing. Tonight he shows you the frame hanging in the booth, its glass cracked and taped from behind. He had been ashamed, he says, that a pupil could afford such a gift when he could not afford to stay. You notice how carefully he has kept it dusted. You were nineteen, Talon, you tell yourself, and quick to read silence as a verdict. Below the booth, the curtain parts on an empty house.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the younger self's reaction to Lior's gesture?
options: Rueful self-criticism for having mistaken a private shame for contempt.
Lingering resentment that Lior never explained his silence much sooner.
Proud satisfaction that the gift has been carefully preserved for years.
Nostalgic delight in fond memories of the old chemistry classroom.
g.explanation: 과거의 Talon은 선물을 엎어 놓은 행동을 모욕으로 받아들이고 연락을 끊었지만, Lior는 그것이 자신의 부끄러움 때문이었다고 밝힌다. 서술자는 '열아홉이었고 침묵을 판결로 읽는 데 성급했다'고 스스로를 돌아보며 후회 섞인 자기비판을 보인다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B의 원망은 남아 있지 않고, C와 D는 과거 반응에 대한 태도가 아니다.

seed.relationship: a young apprentice and a master carpenter
seed.conflict: after a harvest, voyage or season that went badly
seed.topicSeed: a train-station cafe in Vienna; a young apprentice and a master carpenter after a harvest, voyage or season that went badly

g.passage: Vienna's Westbahnhof cafe was where Konrad took me after the worst season of my apprenticeship, the autumn three of our staircases came back warped from a client's damp villa. I was twenty-two then, Camryn the American who measured twice and still cut wrong, and I expected a lecture. Instead he ordered two coffees and spent an hour describing his own first ruined commission, a cabinet that split in its first winter. I have since heard people praise mentors who never let you fail, and I find I distrust them a little. Konrad let me fail, then sat beside me among the departing travelers while it hurt. He did not rebuild the staircases for me; he only made sure I knew I could rebuild them. Outside, a night train to Munich was announced in three languages.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward Konrad's way of handling the failed season?
options: Mild embarrassment that Konrad shared such a personal story in public.
Grateful approval of a mentor who allowed failure and then offered company.
Quiet frustration that Konrad refused to repair the warped staircases himself.
Skeptical distance from the idea that a mentor should ever intervene.
g.explanation: 화자는 실패를 막아 주는 멘토를 오히려 조금 불신한다고 말하며, Konrad가 실패하게 두고 아플 때 곁에 있어 준 방식을 높이 평가한다. 꾸짖는 대신 자신의 실패담을 들려준 장면도 그 고마움을 뒷받침한다. 따라서 B가 정답이다. A의 당혹감과 C의 불만은 지문에 없고, D는 화자가 Konrad의 개입(곁에 있어 줌)을 긍정하므로 틀리다.

seed.conflict: while learning to let go of a habit
seed.topicSeed: a stone bridge in Rotterdam; an interpreter and her client while learning to let go of a habit

g.passage: Wet iron and diesel rose from the river the morning Soren asked me to stop translating for him. I had interpreted for him for six years, at every meeting with Dutch buyers, and out of habit I still leaned toward his ear whenever anyone spoke. We were crossing the old stone bridge to the harbor office in Rotterdam when he said, in careful, slow Dutch, that he wanted to make his own mistakes now. I felt something close to grief, which embarrassed me. I, Marit, had built a version of myself around being needed in two languages at once. In the meeting I kept my hands folded and bit back three corrections. Looking back, I am fond of that woman and a little impatient with her: she mistook usefulness for closeness. A tugboat pushed a barge of gravel under the arch as we left.
g.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward her past reaction to Soren's request?
options: Bitter regret that she ever agreed to stop interpreting for him.
Unqualified pride in how gracefully she accepted the sudden change.
Affectionate but critical understanding of her former dependence.
Lasting confusion about why Soren wanted to speak Dutch himself.
g.explanation: 화자는 당시 슬픔에 가까운 감정을 느끼고 부끄러웠다고 회고하며, 필요한 존재가 되는 것에 자신을 맞춰 왔다고 인정한다. 이어 그때의 자신을 아끼면서도 쓸모를 친밀함으로 착각했다며 조금 답답해한다. 따라서 애정과 비판이 함께 있는 C가 정답이다. A의 쓰라린 후회, B의 순수한 자부심, D의 혼란은 지문과 맞지 않는다.

seed.relationship: a stepmother and a skeptical teenager
seed.conflict: over an unfair rule everyone obeys
seed.topicSeed: a bookbinder's workshop in Oaxaca; a stepmother and a skeptical teenager over an unfair rule everyone obeys

g.passage: Why must every book in the workshop be sewn by hand, even the cheap notebooks sold to tourists? Emiliano asked this every Saturday in the bindery in Oaxaca, and every Saturday his stepmother, Emil, said only that it was the rule. A glue gun sat unused on a shelf, a gift from a supplier. One afternoon a tourist returned a notebook she had bought years before, its spine still tight after a flood had soaked her suitcase. Emil said nothing, but she set it on the bench where Emiliano worked. That week he stopped asking and began counting stitches without being told. Outside, a vendor wheeled a cart of corn drinks past the open door, ringing a small brass bell.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A tourist returns a notebook to the workshop after many years of use.
A stepmother uses a supplier's gift to make the workshop more efficient.
Rules that are obeyed without explanation should always be questioned.
A teenager comes to accept a rule once he sees evidence of its value.
g.explanation: 앞부분에서 Emiliano는 손바느질 규칙에 매주 의문을 제기하지만, 홍수에도 튼튼했던 공책이 돌아온 뒤에는 질문을 멈추고 스스로 바늘땀을 센다. 두 장면의 대비가 규칙의 가치를 확인하고 받아들이는 과정을 보여 주므로 D가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, B는 글루건이 쓰이지 않으므로 틀리며, C는 지나치게 일반적이고 지문과 반대 방향의 교훈이다.

seed.relationship: a mother-in-law and a new bride
seed.conflict: about a translation that changes the meaning
seed.topicSeed: a boarding-house kitchen in Addis Ababa; a mother-in-law and a new bride about a translation that changes the meaning

g.passage: Imani had kept the boarding-house kitchen in Addis Ababa for thirty years, and she did not expect her son's new bride to change its rules. On her first morning, Jomo offered to translate the Amharic menu board into English for the foreign lodgers. Imani agreed, then frowned when a guest ordered the gentle stew and complained that it burned his tongue. Jomo explained that the Amharic word meant patient, slow-cooked, not mild, and that she should have chosen better. That evening Imani handed her the chalk herself and stood beside her, naming each dish while Jomo searched for the truest English. Neither spoke of the morning. On the windowsill, a pot of rue leaned toward the last light.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A mother-in-law comes to trust a new bride who weighs words with care.
A foreign lodger complains about the spiciness of a stew he ordered.
A new bride takes over a kitchen against her mother-in-law's wishes.
Families grow closer when they share household duties with one another.
g.explanation: 처음에 Imani는 새 며느리가 부엌 규칙을 바꾸는 것을 달가워하지 않고 번역 실수에 얼굴을 찌푸린다. 그러나 Jomo가 단어의 정확한 뜻을 설명하고 책임을 인정하자, 저녁에는 직접 분필을 건네고 곁에서 함께 메뉴를 고친다. 이 대비가 신뢰의 형성을 보여 주므로 A가 정답이다. B는 일화만 요약했고, C는 시어머니의 뜻에 반한 것이 아니며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

seed.conflict: about keeping a family business open
seed.topicSeed: an abandoned orchard in Port of Spain; an author and her translator about keeping a family business open

g.passage: Although my grandfather's cocoa orchard above Port of Spain had been abandoned for a decade, I still brought Tyrese there when he began translating my book about it. I am Cecile, and I had written the orchard as a ruin, a place my family had been right to leave. Tyrese walked the rows for an hour and came back with a pod split open, the beans inside still pale and sweet. He asked how to translate a word I had used, finished. I said it meant done, closed. He said the trees did not seem to know that. That night I rewrote the last chapter, and in the morning I called my aunt about reopening the drying shed. Rain came in from the gulf by afternoon, drumming on the tin roof of the car.
g.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To describe how the narrator's grandfather first planted and tended his large cocoa orchard.
To show how a translator's question changed the narrator's view of the family farm.
To argue that books about a family's history lose their meaning in translation.
To suggest that any abandoned place can be restored with enough hard work.
g.explanation: 앞부분에서 화자는 과수원을 떠난 것이 옳았던 폐허로 썼지만, 번역가 Tyrese가 'finished'라는 단어의 번역을 묻고 나무들은 그걸 모르는 것 같다고 말한 뒤 마지막 장을 다시 쓰고 건조장 재개를 의논한다. 이 대비가 번역가의 질문으로 가업에 대한 시각이 바뀌는 과정을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 할아버지의 일화가 없고, C는 번역에 대한 주장이 아니며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

seed.relationship: a seamstress and her only apprentice
seed.conflict: when a long silence is finally broken
seed.openingStyle: 구체적인 사물이나 동작으로 시작(관사 The 로 시작하지 말 것)
seed.topicSeed: a seed-saving cooperative in Naples; a seamstress and her only apprentice when a long silence is finally broken

g.passage: Paper envelopes of tomato seed lined the shelves of the cooperative in Naples, where Wilhelmina sewed seed bags on Tuesdays beside Angus, the seamstress who had taught her everything and who had not spoken to her since a quarrel over a torn hem two winters before. They worked side by side, passing scissors without looking up. One Tuesday Angus's hands shook too badly to thread the needle. Wilhelmina threaded it and handed it back without a word. Angus said, quietly, that the hem had been her own fault. After that the two women talked through every Tuesday, mostly about thread. Through the window, a man was hosing down crates of lemons.
g.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: A seed cooperative depends on volunteers who sew the bags for its tomato seed.
An apprentice decides to leave her teacher after a quarrel over a hem.
A small act of help lets a teacher admit fault and end a long estrangement.
People who work together in silence eventually forget their old disputes.
g.explanation: 앞부분은 두 사람이 다툼 이후 2년 가까이 말없이 일하는 모습을 보여 주고, 뒷부분은 Wilhelmina가 바늘에 실을 꿰어 준 뒤 Angus가 자기 잘못을 인정하고 대화가 다시 시작되는 모습을 보여 준다. 이 대비에서 작은 도움이 침묵을 깨뜨렸다는 요지가 드러나므로 C가 정답이다. A는 배경만 말하고, B는 제자가 떠나지 않으며, D는 다툼을 잊은 것이 아니라 잘못을 인정했으므로 틀리다.

seed.relationship: a foreman and a young hire
seed.conflict: over how to describe an accident honestly
seed.topicSeed: a hillside terrace in Taipei; a foreman and a young hire over how to describe an accident honestly

g.passage: Kemoy wrote the report twice. The first version, which Leila the foreman had suggested, said the retaining wall on the tea terrace above Taipei had simply collapsed in the rain. The second said Kemoy had stacked the stones himself, too fast, because he wanted to finish before the last bus down the hill. His father had built walls for forty years and once told him that a wall remembers every shortcut. Kemoy had also watched that same father lose his work for hiding one. He handed Leila the second version. She read it, folded it, and asked whether he had eaten. Below them, a cable car slid silently toward the city.
g.question: Based on the text, why does Kemoy most likely submit the second version of the report?
options: He fears that Leila will discover the truth and dismiss him for lying.
He hopes that confessing will earn him a quick promotion to the foreman's position.
He has learned from his father's experience that hiding a mistake costs more.
He believes inspectors will reject any report that blames the rain.
g.explanation: 지문 중간에서 아버지는 벽이 모든 지름길을 기억한다고 말했고, Kemoy는 아버지가 지름길을 숨기다 일을 잃는 것을 지켜보았다. 이 두 문장을 이어 읽으면 실수를 숨기는 대가가 더 크다는 교훈이 그의 동기임을 알 수 있으므로 C가 정답이다. A의 해고 걱정은 다른 감정에서 나온 동기이고, B는 결과를 동기로 착각한 것이며, D의 검사관은 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

seed.topicSeed: a weaving cooperative in Seville; a daughter and her absent father's friend over unequal sacrifices made in the past

g.passage: I had not meant to stay past dusk in the weaving house, but Alonso kept unrolling cloths my father had once dyed, each a deeper red than the last. He had stayed in Seville to keep the looms running, he said, while my father sailed off after a fortune that never came home. I listened for blame in his voice and found none, only a weariness worn smooth, like the handles of the shuttles. Still, I felt an old ledger open in me: what he had given, what we had taken. He laid the last cloth across my knees as gently as a blanket on a sleeping child. Ingrid, he said, your father chose this red for you. I traced the pattern with one finger, warmed through, and could not say thank you. The lamps along the river were lit one by one.
g.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Uneasy and guilty, with little warmth passing between the two speakers.
Celebratory and proud, honoring the beauty of the cooperative's cloth.
Guilty above all, with only a faint trace of tenderness toward Alonso.
Tender and wistful, though shaded by the narrator's unease over a debt.
g.explanation: Alonso가 아버지가 염색한 천을 아이에게 담요를 덮듯 무릎에 놓아 주고, 화자가 따뜻함을 느끼는 장면에서 다정하고 그리운 정서가 두드러진다. 동시에 '그가 준 것과 우리가 가져간 것'이라는 장부의 비유가 빚에 대한 불편함을 덧붙인다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서만 말했고, C는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었으며, B는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

seed.topicSeed: a soccer field at dusk in Kyoto; a retired sailor and his neighbor after learning how someone really earned their reputation

g.passage: I used to think Chinedu's brass compass was a trophy. He carried it everywhere, even to the soccer field by the river in Kyoto where we watched the boys play until the lamps came on, and the neighbors said he had won it for steering a ship through a typhoon alone. One evening, as the light went orange over the goalposts, he told me otherwise. The captain had steered; Chinedu had been seasick below. The compass was the captain's, given to Chinedu the morning the man died. I, Fumiko, had repeated the heroic story to half the street. He opened the compass and let the needle swing. "It points the same way whether people say true things about me or not," he said. After that, when the boys asked him for sea stories, he told them about the captain. The ball thudded against the post.
g.question: In the text, the compass most likely represents
options: the courage Chinedu displayed while steering through the typhoon.
a steady truth Chinedu holds to regardless of what others say.
the wealth Chinedu gained from his many years working at sea.
Fumiko's eagerness to repeat exciting stories to the neighbors.
g.explanation: 이웃들은 나침반을 태풍 속 영웅담의 트로피로 여겼지만, 실제로는 죽은 선장의 유품이었다. Chinedu는 사람들이 자신에 대해 참된 말을 하든 아니든 바늘은 같은 방향을 가리킨다고 말하고, 이후 아이들에게 선장 이야기를 들려준다. 따라서 평판과 무관하게 지키는 변함없는 진실을 뜻하는 B가 정답이다. A는 소문 속 거짓 용기이고, C의 재산과 D의 화자의 욕구는 근거가 없다.
